newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander's to buy half of Brazil's Noroeste.
newsitem.headline: Santander's to buy half of Brazil's Noroeste.

text.p: Spain's leading bank Santander said Friday its Brazilian unit Banco de Geral has agreed to buy 50 percent of another private Brazilian bank, Noroeste, for about $500 million.

The two bank holdings together will make Santander the seventh-largest private bank in Brazil. Noroeste is a family-owned medium-sized bank with 93 branches and assets of 6.5 billion reais ($6 billion).
The deal will complete Santander's investment plans in Latin America, where it has already invested or agreed to invest more than $1.5 billion this year, Santander said.
"Geral will take control of Banco Noroeste through the acquisition of approximately 50 percent of Noroeste's total share capital," the bank said in a statement.
"Banco Geral's estimated investment in Noroeste will be a maximum of $500 million, which includes all related transaction costs and fees," it said.
Santander's 51-percent owned Banco de Geral is carrying out the operation using its own capital.
Santander agreed in March to purchase Geral for $220 million to be paid over three years.
Santander Chairman Emilio Botin said Noroeste's solid capital base, commercial branch network and client base complemented that of Banco Geral.
The acquisition is subject to approval by the Brazilian and Spanish authorities.
